summary: Add cross-provider multi-city flight search to the `flights` command via a repeatable --segment flag and a --provider switch (kayak | google | auto). Kayak returns real flight prices; Google generates an authenticated-multi-city deeplink (the underlying Google POST requires a cookie jar).
reason: Two providers, two integration shapes: (A) Google Flights' multi-city POST requires an authenticated Google session (SAPISID cookie + XSRF hash); anonymous POSTs return travel.frontend.flights.ErrorResponse regardless of session-token / f.sid / build-string tweaks (verified empirically). flight-goat has no cookie jar, so the Google path generates the canonical multi-city URL via a hand-rolled tfs-protobuf encoder; the URL opens to a fully-prefilled multi-city search where Google's UI handles auth from the user's browser session. (B) Kayak's POST /i/api/search/dynamic/flights/poll works server-side without authentication — only requires CSRF formToken (regex-scraped from the shell HTML) + the session cookies the initial GET sets. Two-phase polling, denormalized response with leg/segment IDs that look up into top-level lookup maps. Default --provider=auto runs Kayak for prices + appends Google URL. The existing tripType=1/2 one-way + round-trip POSTs are unchanged.
validated_outcome: go build ./... + go vet ./... + go test ./... all green. 17 new tests covering Google URL builder (3), one-way regression guard (1), CLI segment parser (4), Kayak URL/body/parser (9). Live smoke tests confirmed: (a) --provider google returns a Google Flights URL that loads the multi-city search page with prefilled dates + IATA codes; (b) --provider kayak returns 50 itineraries (totalCount 1567) for a 3-segment SFO→NRT→ICN→SFO query, cheapest at $1,161 via UA, with bookable kayak.com URLs. govulncheck reports 0 reachable vulnerabilities.
